title.en: Thinkers, economy and links with Southeast Asia

text.en:
Meena saw a picture of the Angkor Wat temple, similar to temples in India.
"Ideas travelled by sea," said her teacher.

Thinkers such as Ramanuja and Basaveshwara taught devotion and equality, and scholars like Al-Biruni wrote about India's sciences. Poets and temple builders created great works.
Economy and administration: kings collected land taxes, guilds of merchants traded widely, and temples were centres of wealth and learning.
The Cholas sent ships to South-East Asia, spreading culture, trade and architecture, seen in temples such as Angkor Wat.

problem.en: How did Indian culture reach Southeast Asia?

text.en: Temples like Angkor Wat show the link.

prompt.en: A friend says India had no links with Southeast Asia. How will you reply?

points.en: India and Southeast Asia were linked.
